# Notion

Notion workspaces and pages, private or published to the web (`*.notion.site` or a custom domain). The customer exports the pages and you work on the export locally. The old pages stay on Notion, so you produce a route table instead of redirects.

## Detect

- Page URLs: `https://www.notion.so/<workspace>/<Title>-<32-hex id>` or `https://<domain>.notion.site/<Title>-<32-hex id>`; published sites can use a custom slug instead.
- A Markdown & CSV export ZIP holds `.md` pages and `.csv` databases whose file and folder names end in a 32-hex page id, with a folder per page that has subpages.
- Markdown pages contain callouts as raw HTML (`<aside>`), because Markdown has no equivalent.

## Get the source

### From the repo

None; use an export.

### From an export

Formats, options and limits: https://www.notion.com/help/export-your-content

- **Format.** Ask for Markdown & CSV with "Include subpages" and "Create folders for subpages" on, and files and images included. HTML is the fallback. Do not use PDF.
- **Scope.** A page export (`•••` → Export) covers that page and, with subpages, its tree. A whole-workspace export is under Settings → General (https://www.notion.com/help/workspace-settings). Either covers only pages the exporting user can access; guests need full access. On Enterprise, owners can disable export.
- **Delivery.** Large exports arrive as an emailed download link that expires. Ask for every part if the export is split.
- **Databases.** A full-page database exports as a CSV of the chosen view plus one `.md` per row. Form views do not export.

Inspect the layout before writing the transformer (`mint migrate --topic discovery`, From an export). Build an id → file index from the id suffix of every file and folder name.

**API alternative.** If the customer prefers, they can run Notion's markdown endpoint (`GET /v1/pages/<id>/markdown`) on their machine with their own integration, shared with the pages in scope. Never ask for the token. Its syntax differs from the export (`<callout>`, `<columns>`, `<synced_block>`, `<page>`, `<unknown>` for embeds and unshared content) and long pages come back `truncated`. Reference: https://developers.notion.com/guides/data-apis/working-with-markdown-content

### From the live site

Public pages render client-side and serve no raw endpoint, so scraping is unreliable. Use an export. Use the published site only to confirm which pages are public and in what order they appear.

## Config → docs.json

Notion has almost no site chrome to carry over.

| Notion                                    | docs.json                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace or root page name               | `name`                                                    |
| Root page icon                            | `favicon` (ask for a logo; page icons are usually emoji)  |
| Site header links (Notion Sites)          | `navbar.links`                                            |
| Several teamspaces or root pages migrated | `navigation.tabs` or `navigation.products`, only as shown |
| Page cover images, fonts, full-width      | drop and report                                           |
| Sharing, permissions, guests              | drop and report                                           |
| Comments, page history, analytics         | drop and report                                           |

## Navigation

The page hierarchy is the navigation. Build it from the export's folder nesting: a page with subpages becomes a nested group whose first page is the parent page itself (`mint migrate --topic navigation`).

- The export does not record sibling order. Take it from the order of child-page links in the parent page body, then the workspace sidebar or published site as the customer sees it; ask if neither is available.
- Map teamspaces or separate root pages to tabs only if the source presented them as separate sections.
- Keep page titles verbatim as labels. Database row pages go under their database's group only if they were navigable pages on the source.

## Content conversion

Count every distinct HTML tag and block pattern in the export before mapping (`mint migrate --topic conversion`).

| Notion export                                         | Mintlify                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Page H1                                               | `title`; remove it from the body                                                              |
| Property lines under the title (database rows)        | drop and report, unless the customer wants them as a table                                    |
| Callout (`<aside>` with an emoji)                     | `<Note>`, `<Info>`, `<Tip>`, `<Warning>`, `<Danger>` by meaning; ask for the emoji → type map |
| Toggle (`<details>` or a nested list item; inspect)   | `<Accordion title="...">`                                                                     |
| Toggle heading                                        | heading followed by its content, or `<Accordion>` if the customer prefers it collapsed        |
| Columns                                               | `<Columns>`, one child per column; unwrap if the content does not fit                         |
| Code block with language                              | fence with the language; caption → title                                                      |
| Equation (`$$...$$`, inline `$...$`)                  | LaTeX, unchanged                                                                              |
| To-do (`- [ ]`, `- [x]`)                              | list; prefix each item with its status                                                        |
| Table, simple table                                   | markdown table; HTML table made MDX-safe if cells hold blocks                                 |
| Synced block (duplicated wherever it appears)         | snippet (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Reusable content)                                 |
| Link to a page (`Title%20<id>.md`)                    | root-absolute path via the id → path index (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Links)         |
| Page mention or link to a page outside the export     | absolute Notion URL; report                                                                   |
| Inline or linked database view                        | markdown table of the CSV, or a list of links to its row pages; report                        |
| Bookmark                                              | link with its title                                                                           |
| Embed (YouTube, Figma, Loom, Google Drive, and so on) | video embed where supported, else a link; report                                              |
| Table of contents block                               | drop                                                                                          |
| Breadcrumb block                                      | drop                                                                                          |

Decode URL-encoded link targets (`%20`) before matching ids. Strip the id suffix from every file name and slug; slugify titles for new paths.

## Assets

- Images and files sit in a folder next to each page, named after the page. Copy them to `images/<page-path>/` (images) or a downloads folder (other files) and rewrite references (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Images and files).
- Links to Notion-hosted files (`secure.notion-static.com`, signed `amazonaws.com` URLs) are signed and expire. Download them during conversion, never hotlink. Reference: https://developers.notion.com/reference/file-object
- Notion icons and covers that are emoji or Notion's built-in images are not files; drop them.

## URLs and redirects

Old URLs stay on Notion, so `redirects` cannot catch them. Produce `route-table.csv` as in `mint migrate --from confluence` (URLs and redirects), keyed by the 32-hex page id: `page_id, old_url, new_path, title`. Take `old_url` from the published site or the page's share link; title segments in Notion URLs change on rename, the id does not. If the customer moves a custom domain from Notion Sites to Mintlify, add `redirects` for the old paths instead (`mint migrate --topic navigation`, Redirects). Site settings: https://www.notion.com/help/public-pages-and-web-publishing

## Known gaps

- Databases: views, filters, sorts, relations, rollups, formulas and properties beyond the title.
- Synced blocks no longer sync with Notion; the snippet is the single source from now on.
- Comments, page history, permissions, guests and sharing settings.
- Notion-specific embeds and blocks (buttons, forms, AI blocks, link previews) with no equivalent.
- Pages the exporting user could not access, and pages outside the exported tree.
